document.edit: When the supported contract or instructions change.
document.guard: Keep one authority; preserve historical evidence and private reporting boundaries.
document.validation: Canonical links/identity plus documentation drift; review prose.

policy.edit: Only for a reviewed control or profile change.
policy.guard: Do not weaken rules to silence findings or hand-edit adopted evidence.
policy.validation: Canonical structured-data and the owning focused gate; hosted integrity.

workflow.edit: When triggers, permissions, pins or job contracts intentionally change.
workflow.guard: Use reviewed immutable action pins, least permissions and honest failure handling.
workflow.validation: Canonical action/YAML checks, pinned actionlint and workflow fixtures; see workflow reference.

script.edit: For a scoped CLI/validation implementation change with failure fixtures.
script.guard: Preserve exit/report contracts, boundaries and downstream compatibility; no embedded credentials.
script.validation: Ruff/mypy, named tool fixtures and owning hosted workflow; Tools README.

vba.edit: For reviewed behavior or source-presentation changes.
vba.guard: Preserve export identity/CRLF, component visibility, API and cleanup; annotate variables and phases.
vba.validation: Canonical and focused VBA gates, generated profiles and actual Excel regression.

asset.guard: Keep formats and referenced paths coherent; no confidential screenshots or unrelated binaries.
asset.validation: Canonical artifact/path checks and visual review.

git-policy.edit: For reviewed editor, normalization, exclusion or archive policy changes.
git-policy.guard: Do not convert binary companions to text, normalize VBA incorrectly or commit local secrets.

wiki.edit: When the guided journey or a linked contract changes.
wiki.guard: Keep authority notices, ordered navigation and exact-source publication; no independent online policy edits.
wiki.validation: Wiki source/fixtures, canonical links, documentation drift and separate published comparison.

directory.edit: When adding a component of this directory role.
directory.guard: Keep production, examples, tests, metadata and outputs in their owned locations.
directory.validation: Canonical required-directory/role checks; file-specific gates below.
